newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt to continue RBA waiting game.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt to continue RBA waiting game.

text.p: *Short Australian bond yields were above their initial lows after the Reserve Bank left policy unchanged this morning, but sell-offs are expected to be limited on strong rate cut hopes.
*Bond futures rollover makes up large portion of trade.

Short Australian bond yields were above their initial lows after the Reserve Bank left monetary policy unchanged this morning, but sell-offs are expected to be limited for now on strong rate cut hopes.

"The market is strong and nobody is going to stand in the way of it, whether or not you believe there will be another rate cut. Pullbacks from here are going to be minimal over the next couple of weeks," one trader said.
Thursday's extremely weak labour force data fuelled expectations that the RBA will have to ease policy again, and the market was fully prepared for that to happen today.
Yields edged up after the central bank left policy unchanged at its usual 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time.
"It was definitely a case of will they, won't they before 9.30. They didn't but the market still belives they will sooner or later," one trader added.
September bills settled back on today's stable policy stance, but at 94.89 the market is still practically pricing in a 50 basis point easing in current 5.5 percent official rates.
The three and 10-year bond futures rollover to September from June made up a large portion of the trade ahead of Monday's expiries.

The market showed a widening bias against the dollar bloc after Thursday's sharp narrowing, particularly at the short end after rates were left on hold. Canadian debt was strong on waning fears of a Fed tightening and the 30-year spread to the U.S. went to a negative for the first time.
